Robot forgets everyone here and what you call them, and may learn anyone you removed again. The phone\'s contacts aren\'t touched. This can\'t be undone.
What People and Messages turn on, nothing else

To learn names, Robot looks at the notifications of one messaging app only, and of those only the sender of a one-to-one chat. With Settings › Messages on, it also reads the messages of the apps you turn on there, in memory only. Settings › People and Settings › Messages say what Robot reads, where it is kept, and how to take it back.

Android calls notification access a restricted setting for apps installed from a file instead of an app store, as Robot is: harmful apps installed that way have used it to read people\'s messages and login codes. So it takes three steps.
1. Tap Notification access and turn on Robot\'s access (in a list, tap Robot first). If Android says “Restricted setting”, tap OK.
2. Tap App info, then ⋮ (top right) › Allow restricted settings, and confirm; Android may ask for your PIN or fingerprint. No such item? Android isn\'t blocking Robot: skip this step.
3. Tap Notification access again, turn on Robot\'s access and tap Allow.
What Robot reads, and where it goes

Notification access lets an app see every app\'s notifications. Robot asks Android for conversations only, drops all but that one app\'s at once, and learns nothing from them while this switch is off. Settings › Messages, if you turn it on, uses the same access to read the apps you choose there, in memory only.

From a message in a one-to-one chat, Robot keeps only the sender\'s name and address and which of your accounts got it. It never looks at, keeps or logs what the message says, and group chats teach it nothing. It checks the app\'s signature too, so an app pretending to be it teaches nothing.

Names stay on this phone, in Robot\'s private storage, left out of Android\'s backups. Robot never sends them anywhere by itself: not to a helper, not to any other online AI model. Robot\'s own model, on the phone, sees a name only when it looks someone up for you. Only if you choose to share with a helper a conversation in which Robot looked someone up (Include, a helper you trust with personal content, or Safety & privacy › Send personal content to helpers automatically) can what Robot said about them go with it.
To take it back: turn this switch off, and Robot stops learning at once. Then turn Robot off in Notification access. Names already learned stay until you tap Remove on them, or Delete all People.
They were deleted meanwhile: Robot didn\'t bring them back.
